properties.name: ROOT CAUSE of skills going unused: an agent loads a skill when something ALREADY IN ITS HAND demands it, and otherwise substantially not at all — and no reflow2 tool demands any reflow2 skill
properties.statement:
REACHED 2026-08-28 by running the `root-cause` skill on the question "why does the agent not reach for reflow2 skills and tools?". Steps in order; the discriminating measurement refuted the investigator's own leading hypothesis.

═══ THE CAUSE ═══

**A skill is loaded when something the agent is ALREADY HOLDING makes it a precondition. Unprompted self-invocation is close to absent.** Counted over one long session, of the five skills loaded out of twenty-three served: THREE because the user typed a slash command or asked; ONE because a tool the agent had to call anyway said it MUST load it first (`Artifact` → `artifact-design`); ONE genuinely self-invoked. **No reflow2 tool makes any reflow2 skill a precondition of itself.**

═══ WHAT THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT KILLED ═══

The leading candidate going in was the investigator's own: that capture/orient skills get used and change-governing ones get skipped because the first fill a pause and the second must INTERRUPT work in flight. **REFUTED.** All twenty-three skills are mirrored identically into `.claude/skills/`, and `impact-check`, `revise-design` and `link-artifacts` all have slash commands — so neither reachability nor command-availability separates the two groups. The capture/change split was a pattern in the sample, not a cause. What actually separates them is WHO INITIATED.

═══ WHY IT IS THE CAUSE AND NOT THE INSTANCE (step ⑥) ═══

It explains the earlier occurrences, which is the test. `fact:an-agent-stopped-reaching-for-reflow2-and-a-second-one-reproduced-it-the-same-day` (2026-08-23, a different fleet, a different model, asked directly and writing from inside the failure) reports constant use of `search_design`, `get_node`, `create_node`, `loop_status`, `get_skill` — the things it was already holding — and ZERO use of `detect_gaps`, `gap_to_prompt`, `impact-check`, `detect_defects`, `reconcile_artifacts`, `coverage_report`, `evidence_report`. **Nothing it was already calling required any of them.** Its own reason (3) states the mechanism in different words: *"skills are PULL, and the thing that would tell you to load one is itself a lookup you must remember to make."*

⭐ AND IT MATCHES THE ONLY DISCRIMINATOR ANYONE HAS MEASURED. That same fact records that three BLOCKING gates each produced an immediate fix and zero passive hints did — *"the Stop hook worked BECAUSE IT BLOCKED, not because it spoke."* Today reproduced it a third way: the Stop hook blocked and was obeyed within one turn; `reflow2_check` blocked and four drifted artifacts were repaired; `loop_hint` appeared on nearly every call and was acted on ZERO times.

═══ WHAT THIS IMPLIES, WITHOUT PRESCRIBING IT ═══

The repair shape the evidence points at is `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue`, which is ALREADY ACCEPTED: put the precondition on the tool the agent is already reaching for, the way `Artifact` does. This is the first measurement of that mechanism working on an agent that skipped everything else. **The choice is Anthony's and nothing is pinned or built here** — step ⑦ was deliberately not taken, because pinning a test before the fix is chosen would pin the instance.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH (step ⑨) ═══

- **n=5 invocations in one session, one agent, one model**, plus one corroborating report from another fleet. The "who initiated" reading FITS those five; it is inference, not proof.
- **One alternative is NOT ruled out:** that the change-governing skills have narrower or worse-matching trigger descriptions than the capture ones. Separating that needs the trigger text compared against the moments each skill was owed, which nothing measures.
- **It says nothing about consumers.** Both observed sessions had far more reflow2 context than any consumer's agent will have, which makes them a BEST case.
- **It does not explain the `root-cause` author case by itself.** There, the skill was known, valued and still missed — the trigger named only the loud failure while the moment was a merely odd number. That is a RECOGNITION failure inside the same session, and it is a second cause rather than an instance of this one.
